SECTION II Curricular Matter Which Require Confirmation by the Faculty Senate NEW PROGRAMS: COLLEGE OF EDUCATION AND PROFESSIONAL STUDIES: School of Education: (see Appendix C) B.S. in Early Childhood Education, Pre-K-2 Certificate The Early Childhood Care and Education (ECCE) program for working professionals in the incumbent workforce comprises two pathways: (1) B.S., Pre-K-2 Certification Pathway and (2) Post Baccalaureate, Pre-K-2 Certification only (proposed separately).
Students in these two pathways will be in the same cohort to complete their undergraduate degree with a Pre-K-2 teaching certification and Post Baccalaureate Certificate only program to be certified as a teacher and advance in their teaching profession.

At least 30 hours per week of the incumbent workforce candidate’s active teaching are required; other non-traditional work conditions with RIDE approval can be considered.
The ECCE program will be offered fully online through URIOnline with field experience in the candidates’ own PreK-2 teaching setting, running 7-week accelerated sessions, including a summer session, for 2 years.
The Pathway 1 (BS + Pre-K-2 certification) requires an associate's degree from CCRI (or equivalent pre-academic work) to complete the Bachelor's degree.
The ECCE program is designed to meet the needs of the incumbent early childhood care and education workforce to access high-quality teaching certificate programs in order to improve teacher quality and student learning.
Aligned with the URI mission, the SOE & CEPS strategic plans, and the Early Childhood Care and Education (ECCE) Strategic Plan for Rhode Island, this program is designed to ensure that the incumbent workforce of early childhood educators has accessible, high-quality, and meaningful pathways toward credential attainment, career advancement, and higher compensation.
This program is supported by The RIDE Educator Pathways Planning Grant. 1

4 In the State of Rhode Island, in order to achieve a high-quality rating (4 or 5 stars) on the state’s Quality Rating and Improvement System (BrightStars), child care programs must employ

5 workers with college credits in Early Childhood Education (ECE) and postsecondary degrees.
In addition, childcare programs that seek to become a Rhode Island Pre-Kindergarten provider must employ Bachelor’s degree and Pre-K-2 certiﬁed teachers in order to achieve Comprehensive Early Childhood Education (CECE) program quality approval (RI Board of Education, 2018).
A lack of a trained workforce prevents child care centers from moving up on the BrightStars continuum, from qualifying to become a State Pre-K provider, and from receiving CECE approval.

Critical Thinking and Problem solving (applying inquiry, evidence, discovery, and hands–on engagement with learners); 6.
Classroom management (establishing a safe and secure classroom environment; helping students to be self-motivated); 7.

Working with families (involving families in the school, enlisting their support, keeping continual communication with them); 8.
Communication (using Universal Design for Learning (UDL), tailoring teaching to meet individual needs; 9.
Formal and Informal Assessment (scaﬀolding students to become reﬂective practitioners; setting goals based upon student needs and assessment results); 10.
